Seal and unseal store entries; mark them for deletion

Source: R/save-objects.R
seal.Rd

Store entries update IN PLACE, so finished work can be locked: seal_model("TOPIA") freezes the store entry — re-saving identical content stays a silent no-op, but CHANGED content errors until unseal_model(). A scenario has two parts, sealed separately: its INPUTS (model, settings, interpolated parameters) and its OUTPUTS (runs). seal_scenario(x) seals the inputs and leaves the outputs open: the scenario is never re-saved – scenarios built on it (interpolate_model(base = )) may reference its tables – but it can still be solved under a new run label, and save_scenario() then writes that run alone; runs can be dropped. seal_scenario(x, outputs = TRUE) makes it an archive: no new run, no dropped run. A sealed entry also can never trigger the reference-mismatch warning — its content cannot drift.

The other end of the lifecycle: mark_delete(x, importance = ) queues an entry for deletion (HIGHER importance = more valuable = deleted later), unmark_delete(x) clears the mark, and delete_marked() — dry-run by default — actually removes marked entries up to an importance threshold. Sealed entries are never deleted, even when marked.

All lifecycle state lives in the entry's manifest, so it survives moves and syncs, and refresh_registry() never disturbs it.

Scans the four stores for entries queued by mark_delete() and removes those at or below max_importance. Dry-run by default: it only lists what would go. Sealed entries are never deleted, even when marked (reported as skipped_sealed), and neither are entries that something still references (skipped_referenced). After a real deletion the registry is refreshed.

Usage

seal_model(x, verbose = TRUE)

unseal_model(x, force = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)

seal_repository(x, verbose = TRUE)

unseal_repository(x, force = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)

seal_dataset(x, verbose = TRUE)

unseal_dataset(x, verbose = TRUE)

seal_scenario(x, inputs = TRUE, outputs = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)

unseal_scenario(
  x,
  inputs = TRUE,
  outputs = TRUE,
  force = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

mark_delete(x, importance = 0, type = NULL, verbose = TRUE, version = NULL)

unmark_delete(x, type = NULL, verbose = TRUE, version = NULL)

delete_marked(
  types = NULL,
  max_importance = 0,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  ignore_refs = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

the object (model/repository/scenario), or its registered name. For mark_delete()/unmark_delete() on a bare name, give type =.

verbose

logical.

force

logical; unseal_model() / unseal_repository() refuse while the current sealed version has dependents (see list_dependents()), listing them; TRUE releases the name anyway. The sealed version stays, so the dependents keep loading it. unseal_scenario() refuses while scenarios built on it (interpolate_model(base = )) reference its tables; TRUE unseals anyway, and a later change to it changes them.

inputs, outputs

logical; the parts of a scenario to seal (or, for unseal_scenario(), to unseal). TRUE acts on the part, FALSE leaves it as it is. The inputs are the model, settings and interpolated parameters; the outputs are its runs. Outputs are sealed only with the inputs, and unsealing the inputs opens the outputs too.

importance

numeric; HIGHER = more valuable = deleted later. delete_marked() removes only marks with importance at or below its max_importance.

type

character, the entry type when x is a bare name.

version

for mark_delete() / unmark_delete() on a model or repository: mark (or unmark) superseded sealed versions instead of the whole entry – a hash or prefix, several, or "unused" for every version nothing references (see list_versions()). delete_marked() deletes marked versions that are still unreferenced.

types

character, which stores to sweep (default: all four).

max_importance

numeric threshold; only marks at or below it are deleted (default 0 — the least valuable tier).

dry_run

logical; FALSE actually deletes.

ignore_refs

logical; TRUE deletes referenced entries too. Named apart from force because drop_scenario_run()'s force means something else (the active run).

Value

a tibble of the marked entries (type, name, importance, sealed, dependents, action, path), invisibly when deleting.

Details

Since save_scenario() references the model store rather than embedding a copy, deleting an entry can break the entries that point at it — and the breakage would surface only later, at load time. So a marked entry with dependents is skipped: list_dependents() lists them, and ignore_refs = TRUE deletes anyway.

In an interactive session a referenced entry is offered rather than silently skipped: the dependents are named and the deletion confirmed one entry at a time. A non-interactive session is never prompted — it takes the refusal and ignore_refs, so a scripted sweep cannot hang.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
open_project(tempdir())

save_repository(newRepository("my_repo", newCommodity("ELC", unit = "MWh")))

# sealing and marking address the STORED version, by name: a sealed one
# refuses overwrites and deletion
seal_repository("my_repo")
unseal_repository("my_repo")

# marking is the opposite -- flag now, sweep later
mark_delete("my_repo", type = "repository", importance = 0)
delete_marked(dry_run = TRUE)      # review what would go
delete_marked(dry_run = FALSE)
unmark_delete("my_repo", type = "repository")
} # }
